2026-05-06 (end of day, v1.0.0-beta.1 deep rebrand SHIPPED to origin/main but NOT TAGGED).

DONE THIS SESSION (third session of the day):
- CCLI_PAGER residue sweep committed (3e68d0b) and pushed
- Deep-rebrand spec written and committed (38fa0a8): docs/design-rebrand-deep.md
- Codex updated to reflect rebrand decision: project.identity (KEY NAMING CONVENTION REVISED), project.releasePlan (Phase 2.5 added)
- Dirname .reverie/ verified uncontested
- DEEP REBRAND IMPL COMPLETE (ee11c6c): 163 files changed, +1508/-1336
  * Path resolution: .codexcli/ → .reverie/ everywhere; auto-migration on first walk-up via atomic fs.renameSync; refuses if both old+new exist
  * Env vars hard cutover: 7× CODEX_* → RVR_* (CODEX_DATA_DIR, CODEX_PROJECT, CODEX_PROJECT_DIR, CODEX_NO_PROJECT, CODEX_AGENT_NAME, CODEX_DISABLE_LOCKING, CODEX_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_BYTES)
  * MCP tools hard cutover: 19× codex_* → reverie_* (no shim)
  * Envelope: writes $reverie; reads either $reverie or legacy $codexcli (back-compat preserved indefinitely)
  * Prose sweep: README, CLAUDE.md template, llm-instructions, schema-guide, dogfooding, token-savings, ROADMAP — "the codex" noun dropped, "Reverie" used as a system name
  * Pre-v1.10 .codexcli.json single-file migration path preserved (now converts directly to .reverie/, skipping intermediate .codexcli/ directory format)
  * vitest.config.ts: env CODEX_DATA_DIR → RVR_DATA_DIR
  * Pager: CCLI_PAGER (already done in 3e68d0b)
- This repo's own .codexcli/ auto-migrated to .reverie/ during the test run (side effect of the new path resolver). All git renames preserved by similarity heuristic except 4 entries (epoch + 3 entries that were updated mid-session — show as D + A in git diff).
- CHANGELOG.md [1.0.0-beta.1] section written with full breaking-changes block + migration notes
- CLAUDE.md (this repo's own) rewritten to use reverie_* tools and .reverie/ paths
- Verification gate met: typecheck clean, lint clean, 1392/1392 tests pass (same count as v1.0.0-beta.0 baseline)
- 3 commits pushed to origin/main: 3e68d0b, 38fa0a8, ee11c6c

RELEASE SEQUENCE (current state):
- v1.0.0-beta.0  [SHIPPED 2026-05-06] — surface rebrand
- v1.0.0-beta.1  [CODE LANDED on main 2026-05-06, NOT TAGGED YET] — deep rebrand
- v1.0.0-beta.2  — Phase 2 (Bun commit-phase, short-flag audit)
- v1.0.0 stable

MCP SERVER STATUS (CRITICAL FOR NEXT SESSION):
The MCP server running in Claude Code at session-end was the OLD rvr-beta v1.0.0-beta.0 binary (compiled before this session's rebrand). It looks for .codexcli/ which no longer exists. Any reverie_* / codex_* tool calls in this Claude Code session will misroute to global or fail outright until the MCP is repointed at the new dist/mcp-server.js (or rvr-beta is reinstalled at v1.0.0-beta.1+).
Due to this constraint, the final context.next_session update was hand-written directly to .reverie/context.next_session.json with proper meta.updated timestamp. Hand-editing is normally unsupported but was the only path given the dir migration mid-session.

NEXT SESSION PICKS UP:
- Cut and ship v1.0.0-beta.1 release. Steps:
  1. Bump package.json version 1.0.0-beta.0 → 1.0.0-beta.1
  2. Move CHANGELOG [Unreleased] (currently empty) — section is already at [1.0.0-beta.1]
  3. Commit version bump
  4. git tag v1.0.0-beta.1 (lightweight, per commands.release convention)
  5. git push origin main && git push origin v1.0.0-beta.1 (the tag must be pushed EXPLICITLY — see GOTCHAS)
  6. Watch the release workflow run; verify all 4 platform binaries upload + Homebrew tap auto-updates
  7. Verify install: brew tap seabearDEV/reverie && brew upgrade rvr-beta && rvr-beta -V → 1.0.0-beta.1
  8. SOAK the migration on real data — do at least one real session against a non-trivial existing .codexcli/ store and verify it auto-migrates cleanly to .reverie/
  9. Update Claude Code's MCP server config to point at the new binary so reverie_* tools work
- After soak, decide whether to proceed to v1.0.0-beta.2 (Phase 2: Bun commit-phase + short-flag audit) or jump to v1.0.0 stable

GOTCHAS TO REMEMBER:
- git tag <name> (no -a) creates a lightweight tag. git push --follow-tags only auto-pushes ANNOTATED tags. After git push origin main --follow-tags, also run git push origin v1.0.0-beta.1 explicitly. (Bit us once on v1.0.0-beta.0.)
- The MCP server bundled with Claude Code's session may need reconnect or full Claude Code restart to pick up the new binary. Setting MCP env to point at the new compiled dist/mcp-server.js is the cleanest dev-time approach.

VERIFIED LIVE STATE:
- origin/main: 3 commits ahead of pre-rebrand baseline (3e68d0b, 38fa0a8, ee11c6c)
- Local working tree: 2 untracked files (.mcp.json, bun.lock — both parked)
- This repo's project store: .reverie/ (auto-migrated from .codexcli/ during the impl session)
- Test suite: 1392/1392 passing
- Build + lint: clean

PARKED (do NOT reopen unless user does):
- bun.lock and .mcp.json untracked status (Phase 2 decisions)
- Legacy ccli.rb / ccli-beta.rb formulas in homebrew-reverie (queued for v1.0.0 stable cleanup)
- rvr migrate-claude-md command (post-launch tooling, out of scope for v1.0.0-beta.1)

DON'T (next bootstrap):
- Re-run any completed work in 3e68d0b / 38fa0a8 / ee11c6c
- Cut another release tag autonomously — user-driven moment
- Hand-edit any .reverie/*.json file again — that was a one-time emergency for this end-of-session handoff. Revert to MCP/CLI tools as soon as the new MCP is online.
- Try to use codex_* MCP tools — they were renamed to reverie_*, hard cutover, no shim. The new binary registers reverie_* exclusively.

OPEN THREADS user may pick up next:
- Tag and ship v1.0.0-beta.1 (highest priority — code is on main but not tagged)
- Visual identity (logo, palette, marketing site) — could parallel-track
- Dogfooding Part Three: rebrand-narrative arc, now spans v1.0.0-beta.0 + beta.1
- Triage 3 moderate Dependabot alerts
- Decide legacy ccli.rb / ccli-beta.rb fate before v1.0.0 stable

USER STATE:
End-of-day after a hard push session. Three sessions today shipped Phase 1 + Phase 3 (v1.0.0-beta.0) + Phase 2.5 deep-rebrand code (v1.0.0-beta.1 unreleased). Significant velocity. User explicitly opted to push impl forward in this session rather than defer. Reasonable expectation for next session: verify-and-ship cadence (tag + soak + verify migration on real data).
